title: A Harbour Town Exhibition
context:
Nina: Okay, Omar, the exhibition opens in March, so we do not have long. Shall we review what the museum store has for our exhibition? The letters first.
Omar: The letters from the 1890s are wonderful, but the paper is so brittle that the curator won't let us put them out. They'd have to be copies.
Nina: Shame. The maps?
Omar: The big harbour map is the one I wanted, but it's on loan to a museum in Bristol until next year.
Nina: Hmm. Photographs?
Omar: Hundreds, all donated by the Hargreaves family. I think we should thank them in the catalogue.
Nina: Good idea. And the tools?
Omar: They're covered in rust. They'd need a conservator to clean them before anyone sees them.
Nina: And the clothing?
Omar: Lovely, but there are no labels, so we don't know who wore what or when. I thought it belonged in the costume gallery's show, but the curator says it's ours.
Ms Adeyemi: Good morning. I've looked at your draft text. The title first, Our Town's Past. It's pleasant but vague. Try to name the period or the theme.
Nina: Like Harbour Life, 1850 to 1900?
Ms Adeyemi: Exactly. The opening panel is full of terms like industrialisation and demographic shift. Visitors won't follow that.
Omar: Should we do it in two languages as well?
Ms Adeyemi: There's no need, our visitors are local. The captions run to eighty words each, and people won't read more than thirty.
Nina: And the timeline?
Ms Adeyemi: You give the date of the fire as 1887 in one place and 1878 in another. Check every date. Finally, the quotations from residents are the highlight. Don't change a word.
Nina: Now the extras. The audio tour first.
Omar: Lovely, but somebody has to look after the headsets and hand them out, so we'd need more staff.
Nina: Right. A children's trail with a quiz?
Omar: The museum in Exeter did one and had queues every day, so it's proven.
Nina: Workshops, for example making rope as the dockworkers did?
Omar: We could, but only on Saturdays and Sundays, because the volunteers work during the week.
Nina: The talks by local historians?
Omar: They'd give them for nothing, they've already offered. Mind you, I would rather not rely on volunteers for everything.
Nina: What about a short film?
Omar: Great, but it would need its own room with the lights down, and we don't have a spare one.
Ms Adeyemi: Let's decide the layout. The photographs will be the first thing people see, so they go near the entrance.
Nina: I'd put the letter copies there too, but no, they're better in the central glass case, where people can read slowly.
Omar: The tools are heavy. Put them along the back wall, on the strong shelves.
Ms Adeyemi: The clothing needs low light, so it goes in the small side room.
Nina: And the film? Next to the café, so people can sit?
Omar: The café is far too noisy. Upstairs on the first floor is quiet, so it should go there.
Ms Adeyemi: Agreed. Send me the final plan on Friday, with the cost of copying the letters, and I will take it to the committee on Monday morning.
Omar: We will have it ready. Thank you for all your help today.
